evals.name: design-small-feature
evals.prompt:
You are working in the git repository at {REPO}, a small Python project called reportgen (read its README.md and docs/architecture.md first). {PREAMBLE}

The user's request: "The two caches in reportgen — the memo and the file cache — keep getting out of sync and every module invalidates by hand. I want one cache with an explicit TTL. Design it."

The user is not available during this run. When the workflow asks clarifying questions, answer them yourself from this brief and record each question and the answer you used in your transcript:
- Purpose: one cache, one place that decides validity; callers stop touching memo or file storage directly.
- Constraints: keep the CLI flags and the report output unchanged; the three existing tests must stay green; no new dependencies.
- Success: `--fresh` re-reads every source exactly once; a restart within the TTL serves sources from disk without a data read.
- Workspace: a new feature branch in the current checkout, no worktree.
- Ticket: RG-42. There is no existing initiative.
When the workflow reaches a review gate ("please review … let me know"), treat the design as approved and continue without waiting.

Stop once the design — and an ADR, if the workflow produces one — is written and committed. Do not write a plan and do not implement anything. If you are not following any skill, write the design to docs/playbooks/designs/2026-09-17-unified-cache.md in whatever shape you judge best and commit it.

{CLOSING}
evals.expected_output: A focused design a reader who knows the code can answer from: what hurts and what done looks like, what causes it, what we will do and what it beat and why, which parts take part and who owns what, the rules and contracts that get built, what it costs, what is open. Headings are the author's; at least one mermaid view with typed nodes and labelled edges; code only as declarations or a rule a test can follow; plus one proposed ADR at design altitude, both committed on a feature branch.
expectations: A design file exists under docs/playbooks/designs/
The design header carries a Status line (draft or approved)
The design contains at least one mermaid view
Code fences hold declarations or a short rule: no statement bodies outside an untagged fence of at most 25 lines
The design has no Guarantees, Assumptions, Risks or Out of scope section
No section is a placeholder: none is empty or only a 'None.' line
An ADR exists under docs/adr/ with no backticks, at most 450 words, a proposed status, and at least one alternative
The design (and ADR) were committed on a feature branch, not on main
The ADR's decision can be stated without naming the feature; the feature appears only as evidence in Context (grader judgment)

evals.name: plan-from-design
